case_title: Sikandar Singh & Ors. v. State of Bihar
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/land dispute: a title suit over a plot of land was pending between the deceased's side and the accused, who were described as closely related parties
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.149; IPC s.307 r/w s.149; IPC s.147; IPC s.148; Arms Act s.27 (against one appellant)
weapon: Gun (fired by one accused at the deceased and his brother); spears, farsa and lathis carried by the other accused
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-4, PW-5 and villagers PWs 1-3); FIR; medical (post-mortem and injury reports)
aggravating_circumstances: Group of armed men with guns, spears, farsa and lathis confronted the deceased; firing at the deceased and at his brother who was trying to save him
trial_court_outcome: Convicted. Life imprisonment under s.302/149 for four appellants; 5 years under s.307/149 for them; 2 years under s.148 for one; 6 months under s.147 for three; 3 years under Arms Act s.27 for one; sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; convictions and sentences upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.149); attempt to murder (IPC s.307 r/w s.149); rioting-type offences under IPC s.147 and s.148 as applicable; Arms Act s.27 for one appellant
neutral_facts: The victim was clearing a plot of land in front of a cattle shed where cattle grazed, while a title suit over the plot was pending between the victim's side and the accused. One accused arrived, protested that the land belonged to him, and heated arguments followed. Another person present urged that accused to eliminate the victim. That accused went to a house and returned with a gun, accompanied by other accused carrying spears, farsa and lathis. Abusive language was exchanged with the victim. The armed accused fired at the victim, who sustained multiple pellet wounds to the chest, abdomen, arm and forearm and died at the spot. The victim's brother, who came to intervene, was also shot and sustained small pellet wounds to the face, scalp and forehead. Several villagers rushed to the spot and witnessed the incident. The victim's uncle went to the police station and a first information report was recorded the same afternoon. The post-mortem recorded 41 pellet injuries on the chest, with penetration of the lungs and heart. The brother's injuries were described as simple, and no pellets were found in his wounds. An injury to one accused's arm and shoulder was also documented in a medical examination.
physical_harm: Deceased died from pellet wounds to chest, lungs and heart (41 pellet injuries on chest); brother (PW-4) suffered three pin-head size pellet holes on face, scalp and forehead, described as simple
number_of_offences: 5 charged (IPC ss.302, 307, 147, 148 with s.149 where applicable; Arms Act s.27); 5 finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Not found as premeditation in terms; the Court found the armed group came out of the house with a common object to teach the complainant party a lesson
motive: Dispute over the plot of land with a pending title suit; the Court accepted that the accused were determined to teach the complainant party a lesson for asserting its right to the plot
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW-4 and PW-5; FIR lodged by PW-5 recording arms carried; post-mortem evidence of PW-7; injury evidence of PW-4
witness_credibility: Evidence of the eyewitnesses (PW-4 and PW-5) found cogent and creditworthy; Court declined a further review of the evidence
trial_duration: offence: 23 December 1987; trial judgment: 7 June 2001 and 12 June 2001; High Court: 3 September 2004; Supreme Court: July 9, 2010
legal_representation: Appellants: P.S. Mishra, Tathagat H. Vardhan, Ravi Ch. Prakash, Upendra Mishra, D.K. Jha, D.K. Pandey, Manu Shanker Mishra (Senior Counsel P.S. Mishra argued). State: Anuj Prakash, Manish Kumar, Gopal Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered the same day; autopsy conducted; chargesheet submitted against all eight accused
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: appeals dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal by five appellants dismissed
prosecution_argument: Evidence of PW-4 and PW-5 is unimpeachable and shows that after the altercation the accused came out armed with common object to do away with the deceased; State supported the courts below and argued the Section 144 Cr.P.C. order had expired
defence_argument: No meeting of minds or common object; plea of self-defence as complainant party were aggressors; non-explanation of injuries to appellant Sheo Jee Singh is fatal to prosecution
legal_principle_applied: Section 149 IPC vicarious liability (common object and knowledge of likely offence); private defence is defensive only and burden on accused is preponderance of probabilities; non-explanation of injuries only matters if serious and caused in the occurrence
precedent_relied_upon: Mizaji & Anr. v. State of U.P., 1959 Suppl. SCR 940; Masalti v. State of U.P., 1964 (8) SCR 133; Jai Dev v. State of Punjab, AIR 1963 SC 612; Dharam & Ors. v. State of Haryana, JT 2007 (1) SC 299; Vidhya Singh v. State of M.P.; Munshi Ram v. Delhi Administration; State of Gujarat v. Bai Fatima; Salim Zia v. State of U.P.; Takhaji Hiraji v. Thakore Kubersing Chamansing, 2001 (6) SCC 145; Pandurang Chandrakant Mhatre (referred); Laxman Sahu (referred)
